sections.h2: Why is Evans County so small, and where does it sit?
sections.html:
Evans is the smallest county in this Census comparison on both counts, with 183 square miles of land and a July 2025 estimate of 11,028 residents. It sits on Georgia's coastal plain, with the Canoochee River as its main waterway, and since 2023 it has been part of the Statesboro micropolitan area. Claxton is the seat and the largest city, and Bellville, Daisy and Hagan are the other three (Wikipedia).

The QuickFacts table lists population growth of 2.3 percent since the 2020 base, a $138,200 median home value, $719 median gross rent, and a household income median of $53,259. Owners live in 65.4 percent of homes. Only 25 building permits were issued in 2025, so most buyers are looking at existing houses.

sections.h2: What is the story behind Evans County's creation?
sections.html:
Voters ratified a constitutional amendment on November 3, 1914, that carved Evans out of Bulloch and Tattnall counties. Supporters wanted a nearer courthouse, more office jobs and more hotels and eating places, and some thought a minority in Reidsville controlled Tattnall. The Savannah and Western Railroad created stations that grew into Bellville, Claxton, Daisy and Hagan.

The current neoclassical courthouse in Claxton was finished in 1923. In July 1940 the federal government bought land for Camp Stewart, later Fort Stewart, and an estimated 1,500 people were displaced across the counties involved. Evans Memorial Hospital opened in December 1967, and the Evans County Heart Study ran from 1958 to 1995.

Wikipedia names Claxton Poultry Company, Valmont Newmark, the Georgia Department of Corrections, Camellia Health and Rehabilitation and Pinewood Christian Academy among the larger employers.

sections.h2: How do you reach the Evans County tax offices?
sections.html:
The Tax Commissioner works from Claxton, and the Tax Assessor shares a county phone line with it. The commissioner's department page gives the street address and hours.

  • Tax Commissioner: 201 Freeman Street, Suite 4, Claxton; mail to P.O. Box 685; phone 912-739-1147; open 8:15 to 4:30 on weekdays.
  • County main line: 912-739-1141, with option 1 for the commissioner and the assessor; the contact page lists 8 to noon and 1 to 5.
  • Records: parcel and exemption information appears on the assessor's qPublic pages.

Because the staff is small, the property FAQ asks customers to fax or email documents and wait for a reply, though you may also visit to look through records. Use that route early if you want a payoff before closing, since lines fill up near the deadline.

sections.h2: What does Evans County charge when taxes are late?
sections.html:
The county's FAQ is brief. Taxes are due December 20 each year. A month of delay adds 1 percent interest, and a single 10 percent penalty lands once 90 days have passed.

Evans County property tax FAQ: due date, late charges and lien
StepWhat the county says
Due dateDecember 20 each year
Interest1 percent added every month after the due date
PenaltyOne-time 10 percent after 90 days
Lien (fi. fa.)Filed on the Execution Docket with the court clerk once taxes are past due

The county warns that a fi. fa. can hurt your credit for up to seven years. It also explains its escrow position: the bill goes to the owner, since the commissioner cannot tell who holds a mortgage or whether an escrow account pays the tax. Lenders ask for amounts each year, and the office suggests you keep your bill.

sections.h2: How do Evans County assessments and appeals run?
sections.html:
The Board of Tax Assessors sets values, and an owner who disagrees with a change has 45 days from the notice date to appeal. Per the assessor's exemptions page, a case the board leaves unchanged goes automatically to the County Board of Equalization for a hearing.

Arbitration can replace that hearing, and superior court is the next step after either. The page limits appeals to three grounds:

  • Whether the property is taxable at all.
  • The value placed on it.
  • Whether that value is uniform with similar properties.

A complaint about the size of the tax bill is not a ground, because the bill follows from the millage rate. The Department of Revenue says the appeal must be postmarked inside the 45 days, so mail it early. Assessed value is 40 percent of fair market value.

sections.h2: Which exemptions and land programs does Evans County list?
sections.html:
Evans takes homestead applications at the Tax Commissioner's office from January 1 to April 1, and a granted exemption renews itself. You must own and occupy the home on January 1. A new filing is needed after a transfer of ownership, a name or spelling fix on the deed, or a switch to a different exemption.

The assessor's page, which still shows older income figures, lists a $2,000 standard exemption off the assessed value, $4,000 for owners 65 and older within an income test, an added school exemption up to $10,000 for owners 62 and older, and $50,000 for qualifying disabled veterans and unremarried surviving spouses. Ask the assessors for current income limits. Owners 62 and older with gross income of $15,000 or less may defer tax until ownership changes.

Land has its own track. Conservation Use needs an application by April 1, a $10 recording fee and a 10-year covenant, and breaking it can bring a penalty of twice the taxes saved. Freeport applications are due by April 1 as well.

sections.h2: What should an Evans County seller do before closing?
sections.html:
Ask the commissioner for a payoff in writing, then hand it to whoever runs your closing. Past-due years come first, and the contract decides who covers the current bill.

  • Pay off any fi. fa. so a lien does not surface in the title search.
  • Send the commissioner the new owner's mailing address after the deed is recorded.
  • If you hold an escrow account, tell your lender to close it.
  • Keep a copy of your warranty deed, since the court clerk can supply recorded copies.

Land adds one more step. If the acreage is in Conservation Use, the assessor's page says a buyer who keeps the original use may sign the covenant without penalty, while a change in use during the ten years triggers every penalty.

sections.h2: Why might an Evans County seller choose a cash buyer?
sections.html:
A cash buyer who takes the house as is can skip repair negotiations, which helps when a tax bill or lien already sits on the parcel. Retail sales per capita reached $21,195 in 2022, the highest among the four counties, though 22.6 percent of residents are in poverty and 13.4 percent are Hispanic or Latino.

The right route depends on how fast you need to close and how much work the house needs. Whichever way you sell, the commissioner's payoff comes first.

faqs.q: When does Evans County expect payment of the annual bill?
faqs.a: December 20 each year, per the county's property tax FAQ. After that, 1 percent interest is added monthly. A 10 percent penalty is added once, after 90 days.

faqs.q: Does the Evans County Tax Commissioner mail my bill to the lender?
faqs.a: No. The bill goes to the owner, because the commissioner does not know who the lienholder is or whether escrow exists. Lenders request the amounts directly each year.

faqs.q: How much time do I have to contest an Evans County value?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the date of the notice of change. File with the Board of Tax Assessors. If nothing changes, the case goes to the Board of Equalization, or you may choose arbitration.

faqs.q: What does a fi. fa. mean on an Evans County parcel?
faqs.a: It is a tax lien the commissioner files on the Execution Docket with the court clerk when taxes are past due. The county says it can affect your credit for up to seven years, so clear it before you sell.

faqs.q: Where do Evans County homeowners file for homestead?
faqs.a: At the Tax Commissioner's office in Claxton, between January 1 and April 1. Call 912-739-1141 and press option 1. Once granted, the exemption renews each year unless ownership changes.
